releases.name: v0.18.1: Multi-account documentation
releases.body:
### Documentation

- README: guide for single vs. multi-account usage, a settings table, and a
  "what's new in 0.18.0" section. No code changes.



**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/felipesotero/opencode-hard-limit/compare/v0.18.0...v0.18.1

releases.name: v0.18.0: Multi-account quota, 429 handling and warm
releases.body:
With a single account nothing changes: no new setup, same `threshold`.

### Added

- Multi-account quota: named Claude profiles and OpenAI/Codex account stores are
  read per account, the gate checks the account that serves each request, and
  the sidebar shows one row per account.
- `warm` and `warm --watch` commands that keep idle Claude profiles logged in
  by refreshing their OAuth tokens. Opt-in: they never run unless called.
  `warm` refreshes only expired profiles, with per-account backoff, and runs
  its child process with isolated args, a clean environment and group kill.

### Changed

- A server-sent `Retry-After` on a 429 is capped (`maxRateLimitBackoffMs`,
  10 min; `noBaselineRateLimitBackoffMs`, 1 min when there is no earlier
  reading), and good data keeps being served through the blip.
- A transient error (timeout, 5xx, malformed response) no longer blocks on its
  own. The gate keeps using the last good reading and blocks only when that
  reading is below the threshold, or is too old and close to it
  (`staleBlockMarginPct`).
- A named Claude profile whose OAuth token has expired is allowed through with
  a warning, so the call itself can renew the token.
- `~/.claude` is no longer treated as an extra account beside named profiles.
- Quota account resolution is unified between the gate and the library.



**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/felipesotero/opencode-hard-limit/compare/v0.17.0...v0.18.0

releases.name: v0.17.0: Star prompt, Anthropic multi-account credentials and packaging fix
releases.body:
### Added

- `init` and `install` ask once, on an interactive terminal, whether to star the
  repo on GitHub. Starring needs an explicit yes and goes through your own
  authenticated `gh`; the plugin handles no GitHub token. Skip it with
  `--no-star`, `OPENCODE_QUOTA_NO_STAR=1` or `CI`.
- Tiered Anthropic credential resolution for `opencode-anthropic-multi-account`:
  reads its `accounts.json` first, falls back to OpenCode's `auth.json`, and
  keeps the legacy `claude` CLI/keychain path for single-account users. Cache
  entries are stamped with an account key, so switching accounts forces a fresh
  read. New config: `anthropicAccountsFile`, `anthropicCredentialSource`.

### Fixed

- The published CLI crashed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` because `lib/star.js`
  was missing from the `files` allowlist of the tarball.
- The star prompt no longer appears on `set`, only on `init` and `install`.

### Tests

- `test/package-files.test.js` checks that every relative import reachable from
  `bin/cli.js` and `quota-hard-stop.js` is listed in `files`.



## What's Changed
* Ask once, on install, whether to star the repo on GitHub by @roalhadeff in https://github.com/felipesotero/opencode-hard-limit/pull/2

## New Contributors
* @roalhadeff made their first contribution in https://github.com/felipesotero/opencode-hard-limit/pull/2

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/felipesotero/opencode-hard-limit/compare/v0.15.0...v0.17.0

releases.name: v0.15.0: Global CLI install on startup
releases.body:
### Added

- When the server plugin starts, it installs the matching published package
  globally in the background, so `opencode-hard-limit` is available in OpenCode
  shell mode (for example `opencode-hard-limit postpone 30`).



**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/felipesotero/opencode-hard-limit/compare/v0.14.3...v0.15.0

releases.name: v0.14.3 — Fail-postpone mode
releases.body:
## Fail-postpone mode (new, opt-in)

A third quota-block failure mode alongside fail-closed/fail-open: manually
and temporarily bypass an otherwise-legitimate block when you've decided to
accept the risk of running over quota for a while.

- New `allowPostpone` config flag (`--allow-postpone`, `OPENCODE_QUOTA_ALLOW_POSTPONE`), disabled by default.
- New CLI: `opencode-hard-limit postpone [minutes]` (default 30, clamped 1-240) and `opencode-hard-limit postpone --clear`.
- Runs entirely via OpenCode's native shell-escape (`!command`) — no LLM call, no token cost.
- When enabled, a block's error message and the sidebar widget both surface a hint on how to postpone.
- `opencode-hard-limit get` shows whether a postpone is currently active and how much time is left.

## Fixes

- Sidebar widget crashed entirely on OpenCode restart because the deploy step
  didn't ship `lib/postpone.js` alongside the sidebar plugin — fixed.
- Simplified the quota-block error message; removed AI-directed instruction
  text that had no effect (a blocked subagent's `chat.params` throw happens
  before any model text is generated, so OpenCode's `task` tool has nothing
  to relay to the parent — documented as a known upstream limitation in the
  README instead of working around it with unreliable message text).
- Clarified that OpenCode's shell mode only triggers when `!` is the first
  character *typed* into an empty prompt — pasting the whole
  `!opencode-hard-limit postpone 30` line at once does **not** switch modes.
  The block message, sidebar hint, and README now instruct: type `!` first,
  then paste just `opencode-hard-limit postpone 30` (without the `!`).

## Docs

- New README "Fail-postpone mode" section: how to enable, the shell-escape
  mechanism, the type-then-paste caveat, and the subagent limitation.

**Full diff:** v0.12.2...v0.14.3
